title: Ageing Markdown on a Northbeam Renew Trade-In Offer Once Erasure Has Begun
content:
The ageing markdown follows the days the offer has aged and whether the retailer has already begun to sanitise the batch, since a batch whose serials have begun to carry erasure certificates cannot be sent back whole and its offer follows the market as it now stands, while a batch that could still go back whole is offered without an ageing markdown. Whether erasure has begun is read from the erasure certificates standing on the Renew trade-in agreement's own history: one or more such certificates is an erasure certificate already standing recorded on the agreement.

The deep ageing days are 21 days and the ageing days floor is 7 days.

| The days the offer has aged | An erasure certificate already standing recorded on the agreement | The ageing markdown |
| --- | --- | --- |
| more than 21 days | yes | the stale markdown, 12 per cent |
| more than 7 days but no more than 21 days | yes | the standing ageing markdown, 6 per cent |
| no more than 7 days | either way | none |
| any number of days | no | none |

**Both sides of the two day figures.** An offer that has aged exactly 21 days has not aged more than 21 days, so with a certificate on record the markdown is 6 per cent and not 12 per cent. An offer that has aged exactly 7 days has not aged more than 7 days, so no markdown is applied even with a certificate on record. An offer that has aged 8 days with a certificate on record is marked down 6 per cent.

**Hypothetical illustration.** A batch whose offer has aged 30 days and which carries 2 erasure certificates is marked down 12 per cent. The same batch with no erasure certificate on record carries no markdown at all, however long the offer has aged.
